nary_nodes.label: Oil price sharp fall due to US-Iran attack pause
evidence: The price of oil has fallen sharply on hopes that a pause in attacks between the US and Iran could help to de-escalate the conflict.
Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point, marking a sharp turnaround from last week when it had risen above $100.
The fall came after the US ambassador to the UN said attacks on Iran had been halted for a second night in a row to give "talks some space".
An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A significant change in the market value of a commodity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Example describes a price change event; no schema.org class exists for this, so minting under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Oil price surge due to Iran war outbreak
evidence: The outbreak of the Iran war triggered a sharp rise in oil prices as the conflict led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route which usually carries about 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG).
nary_nodes.type_definition: A rise in the market value of a commodity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Example describes a price surge as an event; no schema.org match, so minting under Event.

nary_nodes.label: US-Iran agreement to halt military operations
evidence: When Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in June to halt military operations and reopen the strait, the price of oil fell back to pre-war levels of around $70 a barrel.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A formal agreement to halt military operations between parties.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Example is a military cessation agreement; no schema.org class exists, so minting under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Collapse of US-Iran ceasefire
evidence: However, the collapse of the ceasefire earlier this month reignited fears over global energy supplies and pushed the oil price back up.

nary_nodes.label: Winter supply risk analysis by Wood Mackenzie
evidence: The wholesale price of gas has also been rising recently, and analysis from research group Wood McKenzie published last week said European gas storage was at a historic low, with supply security for this winter "at risk".
If the Strait of Hormuz remains closed for a further two months, it said storage will end up lower than 70% by 1 November, compared with a five-year average for that date of 90%.

"Low European inventories, strong Asian demand and limited new LNG supply growth almost guarantee elevated prices through this winter and into 2027," said Massimo Di Odoardo, vice president of gas and LNG research at Wood Mackenzie.
